output.summary: A grass-like flowering plant native to central and southwestern Texas and northeastern Mexico, Texas sotol has a small crown and long foliage. Indigenous peoples pit-bake its crowns, then dry and pound them into bread flour; its fermented inner cores are also used to make sotol.
output.edibilityNote: Indigenous peoples pit-bake crowns for bread flour; fermented inner cores have historically been used to make the alcoholic drink sotol.
